Gaming / Play together

Make friendly competition actually friendly

A few house rules can keep the rematch worth having.

✳
The Offbeat EditCulture Issue · 1 min read

IN THIS STORY

Agree on the kind of matchKeep the room in viewLeave room for another nightMore from Gaming

Agree on the kind of match

Ask whether the group wants a close contest, a chance to practise, or a chaotic party game. People can enjoy competition for different reasons, even at the same table.

Choose settings together and explain unfamiliar rules before the first round. Surprising someone with a hidden house rule rarely makes a match more welcoming.

Keep the room in view

Notice whether everyone is getting a turn and whether the jokes still feel shared. A skilled player can offer tips when invited instead of commenting on every mistake.

Take a break when frustration starts to replace the fun. Switching teams or changing games can do more for the evening than insisting on one last decisive match.

Leave room for another night

Celebrate a good play without making someone’s loss the centre of the conversation. A memorable contest can still end with everyone feeling included.

If a rule caused confusion, decide how to handle it next time. A clear agreement is better than carrying an argument into the rematch.

“A few house rules can keep the rematch worth having.”
